item.title: SCP-5755:
item.content:encoded: ok, I like it, the concept is solid the masterful mix of hinting at what he did without actually telling the reader is good I'm going to guess based on Jason's actions and the history of the object given he was responsible for the house fire? my only issue is the 2nd log, In the 1st log I can brush off the behavior of the researchers as just their characters, in the 2nd one I doubt any foundation personnel could get away with the outburst Dr. Greves gives also Jason's character is weird. he's very distressed and vulnerable one moment, invoking sympathy, and the next he's a boomers version of an edgy 14-year-old give it a read through again and polish up the dialogue. But since I enjoyed it so much I'll give you an upvote in good faith that you will fix it up.

item.title: Director Bold's Proposal-J: -1 then +1 so technically +2
item.content:encoded:
Currently, the only known way of preventing SCP-001-J-EX-D-ARC-1 instances from viewing documentation is to erase it entirely, then place [REDACTED] or [DATA EXPUNGED] where it used to be. Alternatively, one can simply █████ ██████████ ████ ███ ████.

This line, I feel, is the most iconic piece of -j literature on the site. Absolutely astounding.

item.title: SCP-5290:
item.content:encoded:
A few nitpicks to your nitpicks

Councilmember as a single word exists and is used correctly.

Transparent objects can be colored? Like, you know, colored glass, plastics and whatnot. Color doesn't make an object inherently not transparent. It could've been a transparent blue prism, for example

Sometimes redactions and expunged data is used to get rid of unimportant information that doesn't really matter to the story, like the amount of dollars earned by use of an anomaly.

item.title: SCP-3790-J:
item.content:encoded: I initially downvoted because I didn't laugh once, but I did appreciate all the cute references left and right and how charmingly crafted it all was. Humor is subjective, so I'll acknowledge quality when I see it, even if it doesn't tickle me personally. Despite me acknowledging the quality, I'm still disappointingly un-tickled, so, No-vote. item.title: SCP-682: Re: why are they trying to kill it
item.content:encoded:
One modern theory rooted in a couple different branches of site lore is that there's some sort of stealthy compulsion effect at work, and/or that there's a deeper reason that 682 has to suffer endlessly.

There's also the fact that it escapes regularly and kills a bunch of people even if they don't try to kill it, so it's worth a shot on the off chance that something works.

item.title: SCP-3030:
item.content:encoded:
Too many words. That surmises the sticking issue of the article.

Both containment and description are unnecessary lengthy, usually to throw unnecessary badassery, redundant information or some flourish. Not all, but most references to O5s and MTFs can be removed here.

After trimming down the text, add paragraphs on the incident description to make it more readable and explain if the Central Plaza is within the five -2s or in the non-affected sectors.

Otherwise this was a very good SCP. To me it is more interesting than 2000 as a Thaumiel-ish thing.
